# MIX native child custody, first non-executable slice

This separate packet persists a native parent/child candidate and prepared outbox. It does not enable mixed execution. The existing single-provider graph refusal, root `START_CONFIG`, workflows, broker, credential callbacks and browser routes are unchanged.

The repository accepts three own-data native IDs and a genuinely opened PostgreSQL owner. It captures both immutable operation proposals, concrete plan rounds, original plan evidence and artifact metadata; exact current human requester/approver membership, recorded policy requirements and approvals; scoped product revision graphs; separate current verified native connections, provider/account/region and derived backend identity; native parent claim and retained root-start metadata. A recorded parent environment fence must match the actual live owning lease. A parent waiting for its separately scoped child can have both lease fields NULL, never a partial pair.

The child graph must be an exact stable-address/spec/provider/region/native-type/ownership/dependency subset of the mixed parent graph. Full parent and child node digests retain their distinct environment labels. This first slice supports source-free non-service graphs; Git/build source acquisition remains the existing private source/custody path. It does not reinterpret a sanitized plan or artifact digest as authenticated original bytes.

The transaction locks operation IDs in lexical order, captures the current frame, waits separately on the exact existing outbox row, rereads at READ COMMITTED, and repeats the full frame in the final fixed-literal insertion statement. Descriptor retention is idempotent only for the exact candidate. A changed candidate needs another independently authorized operation; retained descriptors, approvals, root history and tombstones are never replaced or deleted. Custody consumes no child approval and changes no operation status.

The descriptor permanently records `executionEnabled:false`, `parentEffectCoverage:unsupported`, `compilerReferenceCoverage:unavailable`, `artifactBytesAuthenticated:false`, `connectionAuthorization:not_minted`, and parent `historyAuthenticated:false`. `retainedRequirementDigest` identifies the recorded policy decision's requirement. This helper does not freshly evaluate policy, mint a scoped broker grant, authenticate raw binary custody, or independently read Temporal raw history. No result from it permits mutation. `reserve` always refuses a prepared or absent child; attempted and acknowledged rows refuse replay.

Schema 14 adds `mixed_child_custody` and `mixed_child_intents` with composite tenant/operation foreign keys, bounded JSON, RLS and no browser policies. Custody is immutable. Prepared-to-attempted UPDATE is prohibited even for service-role DML. The service role has SELECT/INSERT on custody and SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on intents, without DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER. Raw authorized SQL can insert diagnostic attempted/acknowledged states, just as a SQL-state fault fixture can seed them; they are never authenticated child history, executable handles or a public acknowledgment API. Getters return only non-executable metadata, and no retained state enables a second Start.

The registry appends platform 14. The emitted aggregate is a new `0016_platform_core.sql`; accepted `0014_platform_core.sql`, agent `0015_agent_oauth_grants.sql`, every shipped migration body and checksum remain byte-exact. Static generation used the unchanged accepted schema-13 aggregate prefix plus the exact new SQL/checksum and canonical emitter hardening, without loading application modules. Root must verify byte-for-byte canonical emission and real migration/reapplication.

Prepared dependency: accepted migration/tenancy fixture revision 1 (`efa4d2a5`, independent C receipt `052228fc`) supplies the two existing test preimages. All other source remains clean `09301572`. Existing ACL expectations and owning/foreign sweeps remain; new mixed exports have individual native test provenance rather than a blanket exemption.

The mandatory native suite is `native mixed child custody [postgres]` in `tests/controlplane/mixed-child-admission.test.ts`, guarded by `ZENITH_TEST_MIXED_CHILD_CUSTODY_REQUIRED=1` before application imports or hooks. Missing PostgreSQL fails the required run. The controls cover duplicate independent pools, foreign workspace, hostile getters/fake handles, independent child approval, recorded approvals untouched, digest/current role/connection/backend changes, exact live lease checks, an observed three-backend outbox-lock wait, immutable rows, synthetic uncertain/acknowledged tombstones, RLS and grants. Artifact bytes, parent history and human/browser identities in the positive fixture are explicitly synthetic or modeled. SQL retention is the positive result; no genuine Temporal child, real OpenTofu, default worker or cloud effect is claimed.

Author execution: none. Root owns Node 22 compiler/lint, canonical emission, native PostgreSQL and integration checks. Suggested affected command, with the approved owning test URL supplied privately:

```sh
ZENITH_TEST_MIXED_CHILD_CUSTODY_REQUIRED=1 ZENITH_TEST_PLATFORM_PG_URL=<owned-test-url> npm exec vitest run tests/controlplane/mixed-child-admission.test.ts tests/controlplane/migrations.test.ts tests/controlplane/tenancy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Outside-owned follow-ups: exact canonical manifest registration/native schema-14 prerequisites after source acceptance; operator/CI aggregate-file handoff; genuine compiler-complete typed reference inventory; immutable executable mixed parent/browser coverage and exact independently approved child effects; fresh default broker connection authorization and policy evaluation; private raw artifact-byte capture; a genuine parent-child Temporal transport with independently verified history, durable attempted reservation, original receipts and nonreplay recovery; cancellation, outage, changed materialized effects, resume and teardown controls. MIX-01 through MIX-04 remain in progress. This packet stays unmerged until independent review and root execution; it cannot satisfy those end-to-end criteria by itself.
